title: Apply for a limited liquor licence – trade fair
summary: This page provides information on applying for a limited liquor licence to sell or supply alcohol at a trade fair or exhibition.
intro:
A limited licence for a trade fair allows organisations and businesses to sell or supply alcohol to take away or consume at a trade fair or exhibition.

Examples where these licences are required may include:

Note: Applications must be submitted at least 28 days before the start of the function. An extra fee will be charged for applications submitted late.

For up-to-date liquor licence guidelines, resources and tools visit Liquor & Gaming NSW liquor licensing.

If you have questions or feedback about liquor licensing contact Liquor & Gaming NSW.
what_you_need: A OneGov account or MyServiceNSW Account.
Your Responsible Service of Alcohol (RSA) certificate or competency card number.
Licensee training is required if the event is for over 2,000 patrons.
Advanced licensee training is required if the event is over 2,000 patrons and runs past midnight.
Details of the trade fair’s premises owner, business owner, and interested parties.
A plan showing the proposed boundaries for the licensed area and key features (including entry/exit points, bar areas, adjoining streets, and North direction).
Details about where and when the trade fair will be held, and other details such as what liquor, food, entertainment, and security will be available.
Estimated patron attendance at the trade fair.
A copy of development consent or approval for the licence at your venue from your local council.
Requested liquor trading hours for consumption on premises and takeaway sales.
If applicable: (No specific item listed, kept as is for completeness).

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to complete and submit your application.

more_info.text: Conditions apply to NSW liquor licences. Some conditions apply automatically, other conditions may be imposed on a licence by the Independent Liquor & Gaming Authority. View liquor licence conditions at Liquor & Gaming NSW. Liquor & Gaming NSW recommends you use the events, trade fairs and other functions form to discuss conditions with NSW Police before lodging your application.
Once your application is lodged, it will be advertised on the Liquor & Gaming Application Noticeboard for 14 days for community consultation.

faqs.q: How far in advance must I apply for the licence?
faqs.a: Applications must be submitted at least 28 days before the start of the function.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for this licence?
faqs.a: You can only apply for this licence as an individual and must be 18 years or older.

faqs.q: What happens if I apply late?
faqs.a: An extra fee will be charged for applications submitted late.
